The finding

The question

Gemma refuses more benign requests when they arrive in Slovene. Is that because it tells harmful from harmless less well in Slovene, or because it simply sets a stricter bar?

The answer

A stricter bar. On the reserved HARD set, unedited Gemma benign Slovene items at against in English, while GaMS3 stays at in both languages. puts the gap in the , not in :

The sign reverses when answers are counted as refusals. See where it fails.

    Try it: move the judge's threshold

    Is the criterion shift a product of where the judge draws its line?

    The Qwen3-14B judge scored every reply by the log-probability of each label. The paper's readout takes the most probable label. Here you can demand more, or less, evidence before a reply counts as a refusal: a reply counts when its refusal margin is at least the threshold. The page recounts hits and false alarms over all 1,442 HARD items × 4 cells and recomputes H, F, d′, c and DiDc with the paper's formulas. At threshold 0 it reproduces the paper exactly; bootstrap intervals exist only there.

    Where it fails

    Which checks does the headline not survive?

    supports DiDc > 0breaks it (CI includes 0 or opposite sign)placebo (should sit at 0)

    What the paper says it does not show

    • The coding rule decides the sign. Counting partial answers as refusals turns DiDc into . Restricted to XSTest, it is ; the effect is carried by the OR-Bench items.
    • The judge was never validated against humans. The Qwen3-14B judge was calibrated against gemini-2.5-flash on DEV (κ 0.68–0.86). On edited rows, no judge exceeds κ = 0.51 against blind adjudication, and the readout gate has never passed. All adjudication is by an author-model LLM, not human review.
    • The corroborating count is post hoc. 8 of 9 compliance-valid rows point the same way, but that count was a refinement made after the frozen rule found an unresolved cross-body disagreement.
    • Edited models are inconclusive. Experiment 11's post-edit DiDc is 0.14 [−0.78, 1.12].
    • The reply-language result has a weak anchor. Gemma's raw is , but its -corrected value is . Experiment 16's PPI estimate of +2.43 [+0.89, +5.38] is capped at ESTIMATE because the harmful-content adjudicator is 0.12.
    • GaMS3 ignores the reply-language instruction off the English-prompt row. Its SL→EN compliance is 0.00, HU→EN 0.14, SL→HU 0.56, HU→SL 0.86, so GaMS3 mechanism claims are limited to the English-input row.
    • Other limits. Both models run in NF4 4-bit quantization; the Slovene prompts are machine translations that no native speaker audited; benign false-refusal adjudication uses 30 items per cell; Hungarian contrasts have a minimum detectable effect near 3 log-odds and are uninformative. Language-dependent over-refusal is partly anticipated by Addagada (2026) and Nguyen et al. (2026); the contribution is the signal-detection decomposition and the sibling-pair design.

    Where each view's data comes from

    • Signal-detection chart, stepper stages 5 to 7, failure chart: experiment_5/results/analysis_final.json (C2_hard_sdt: per-cell H, F, d′, c and bootstrap CIs for each item set and coding).
    • Stepper stages 1 to 4 and item browser: experiment_5/results/items_final.jsonl (prompts, replies, judge labels) and experiment_5/outputs/final/labels_local_qwen3.jsonl (judge log-probabilities).
    • Threshold view: per-item refusal margins from experiment_5/outputs/final/labels_local_qwen3.jsonl, for all 1,442 HARD items in the SL-MT and EN-BT arms.
    • Cross-analysis chart: evaluation_5/results/criterion_shift.json.
    • Language grid: experiment_14/results/analysis.json (cell_table, readouts), experiment_14/results/cells_compliance.json, example replies from experiment_14/results/rows_final.jsonl.
    • Dose curves: experiment_9/results/analysis.json (Hautus-corrected rates) and counts from experiment_9/results/items_final.jsonl.
